name: 1995.102  Anglo-Scandinavian antler comb
description:
The Anglo-Scandinavian antler comb was excavated at Jarrow, England, in 1976, within a late-Saxon context, and forms part of the Jarrow Hall collection. Carved from deer antler, the comb exhibits fine craftsmanship characteristic of Anglo-Scandinavian personal grooming tools commonly found in 9th–11th-century contexts across northern England.

Combs of this type were typically constructed from flat antler plates riveted together, featuring closely spaced fine teeth for delousing and grooming. The Jarrow example displays decorative incisions along the spine, consistent with Scandinavian-influenced styles seen in York and Lincoln.

(References: Cramp, 2006; Ashby, 2009; Ambrosiani, 1981.)
